about: Brotherhood’s story begins in 1839, when John Jaques, a Washingtonville cobbler who had planted grapes behind his shop, released his first commercial vintage. Renamed Brotherhood after its sale to J. M. Emerson & Son in 1886, the winery dug the hand-built underground vaults that still store wine today, kept working through Prohibition by making sacramental wine, and became one of the first places in America to welcome wine tourists. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is now owned with the Chadwick and Castro families of Chile.

Merlot belongs to the premium single-variety range Brotherhood began after 1987, when winemaker Cesar Baeza joined the ownership and the winery started working seriously with vinifera grapes alongside its traditional native-grape wines. The winery buys fruit from independent growers around the state, and describes its Merlot as drawing on the North Fork of Long Island, with a style closer to Bordeaux’s Right Bank than to Napa: plummy and generous, but with backbone, and flavours of dark fruit and herbs. It suits lamb, beef or duck.
facts: Dry, medium- to full-bodied red in a Right Bank Bordeaux mould
